newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates orders Airbuses for $2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Emirates orders Airbuses for $2 billion.

text.p: Dubai government-owned Emirates airline said on Monday it was buying 16 A330-200 aircraft from European consortium Airbus Industrie worth $2 billion.
It has an option for a further seven aircraft, Emirates chairman Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed al-Maktoum told a news conference.
"The new aircraft will gradually replace the present Airbuses from January 1999 until the year 2002," he said.
Sheikh Ahmed said the total cost of the deal with Airbus was $2 billion, including the engines for the new planes.
He said Emirates has not yet decided on the engines. "It is going to be between Rolls Royce Plc and General Electric Co."
Airbus Managing Director Jean Pierson told the news conference that Airbus has "agreed to assist Emirates" with the sale of the Airbuses it currently has.
Emirates fleet includes 16 Airbus A310 and A300s. It recently took delivery of its third Boeing 777 aircraft. It has another four 777s on firm order and an option for seven more.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace -- a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
